title: Sparq runtime sync prep — Kyla personal draft
content:
Context / goals:
- Quick personal prep for the weekly runtime + infra + console sync (Sparq cadence). Quick, actionable — want to keep meeting <= 40m.
- Main aim: finalize canary rollback strategy for v2.3.1 kernels, triage the KV cache regression (seen in prod last 48h), and confirm console metric panels + alerts for next UAT.
- Tone: not a full postmortem; surface facts, owners, and next steps.

Meeting logistics:
- When: Tue 2026-03-16 10:00-10:40 PT
- Where: #serving-runtime huddle room / Zoom link (posted)
- Attendees (requested): Kyla (owner), Omar (infra), Denise (runtime), Mateo (console), Anika (SRE, optional), Luc (QA)

Quick snapshot (what I know right now):
- Observed: KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~67% for 5–20s requests on cluster prod-west-2 between 2026-03-12 03:00–09:00 UTC. Latency P95 increased by ~120ms for impacted routes.
- Canary: v2.3.1 kernel pushed to dedicated-canary pool yesterday; 2 of 6 nodes show increased mem fragmentation in /var. No errors in logs yet, but QPS on canary was low.
- Console: Some dashboards missing the per-route token-cost breakdown after last console front-end rollout (PR #1287). Alerting rule for "kv-hit-drop" is misfiring on staging (false positives).

Agenda (tight, timestamped):
1) 0-5m: quick round — rapid updates (owner)
   - One-liners from each attendee
2) 5-18m: KV cache regression triage (Denise + Omar)
   - Evidence summary (Denise)
   - Recent deploys/change list (Omar)
   - Immediate mitigations (toggle cache TTL, route to older model variant)
3) 18-28m: Canary plan for v2.3.1 (Kyla + Anika)
   - Decision: continue canary vs rollback criteria
   - Define automated rollback thresholds (p95, error-rate, mem fragmentation delta)
4) 28-34m: Console dashboards & alerting (Mateo)
   - Quick fix list for token-cost panel + alert tuning for kv-hit-drop
5) 34-38m: Quick QA/UAT schedule confirmation (Luc)
6) 38-40m: Finish — action item readout + parking lot

Prep notes / facts to have ready (my checklist):
- Logs to pull: kernel dmesg + heap fragmentation logs from 2026-03-12 02:00–12:00 UTC for nodes canary-02, canary-05. (ask infra to attach)
- Metrics: per-node KV hit rate, per-route p95, mem-alloc fragmentation by kernel version. Query saved in Metrics: sparq.kv.hit_rate_by_node (dashboard link).
- Related tickets: RINF-412 (KV hit-rate regression), RINF-398 (console panel regression), RINF-421 (canary rollout notes).
- PR to watch: serving-runtime PR#1287 (console changes) — set to merge hold until panel fix verified.

Open questions I want answered in the meeting:
- Omar: did we change any eviction policy or autoscaler bump on prod-west-2 last week? (I saw a config drift patch in infra repo but need confirmation)
- Denise: is there any recent model change that increases cold-start or buffer usage for the KV layer?
- Mateo: which alert thresholds were updated in the last infra config flip? Can we pin them to absolute counts not relative deltas?
- Anika/SRE: do we have a fast rollback path for kernel variants on dedicated pools? T-shirt estimate for rollback time?

Decision proposals (pre-written so we can vote quickly):
- If KV hit-rate < 75% AND p95 delta > 75ms for > 10m on >2 nodes -> auto-rollout pause + route 30% traffic to v2.3.0 variant. (owner: Kyla)
- For canary nodes, add a mem-frag metric and an alert at frag_score > 0.45. If triggered twice in 30m, rollback canary. (owner: Anika)

Action items (format: action — owner — due):
- Pull dmesg + fragmentation logs for canary-02/05 and attach to RINF-412 — Omar — 2026-03-16
- Add a short-term toggle to route 30% traffic off canary and test p95 — Kyla — during meeting 2026-03-16 (if decided)
- Revert console PR#1287 to wip branch; add token-cost tests — Mateo — 2026-03-17
- Update alert rule for kv-hit-drop to use absolute miss-count and add a 5m suppress window — Mateo + Anika — 2026-03-17
- Run 2x load tests with KV disabled to validate tail-latency boundaries — Luc (QA) — 2026-03-19

Parking lot / for follow-up (not for this meeting unless time):
- Long-term: revisit cache sharding strategy (RINF-330 backlog). Need a design doc draft (owner: Denise).
- Investigate whether the fragmentation is JVM-level or c++ allocator-level for the new kernel path. Might need perf team deep-dive.

Notes to self (Kyla):
- Keep temperature low in meeting — facts first, avoid process blame.
- If we roll back canary, capture metrics baseline immediately after rollback to avoid hysteresis.
- Ping infra on Slack 15m before meeting to ensure logs are attached.

Quick links (for posting in meeting thread):
- RINF-412: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-412
- serving-runtime PR#1287: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287
- Metrics query: https://metrics.redwood.company/dashboard/sparq-kv
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01SRTN8TQ0/p1623445567000300

End of prep. Will convert to tidy agenda and post in #serving-runtime ~30m before the meeting.

-- Kyla
